performanceReview.method: Aggregate windows include complete calendar days. Creative judgment excludes posts younger than 24 hours at 2026-11-03T09:19:58Z. Format comparison covers eligible October 27-November 1 posts. Non-follower reach and Facebook follows unavailable; absent metrics are not measured zeros. No causal attribution from this small sample.
performanceReview.decision: Instagram eligible Reels average 137.5 reach versus 5.2 carousel and 4.67 single; Facebook Reel impressions average 10.67 versus 2 carousel and 2.17 single. No measured Instagram follows. Change hypothesis to recognisable human stakes, clear scale contrast and ordinary household choices, with November 2 single-scene zoom direction; do not extend unexplained physical oddities merely to fill slots.
performanceReview.retiredPattern: Standalone supernatural riddle images with no grounded stakes: three comparable low-reach posts, no measured follows.

performanceReview.baseline: Historical nearly-two-thousand-years post supplied by Thomas is a structural clue (change/conflict/mystery/stakes), not reused text or artwork.

compliance.publicFactualGrounding: Triport coastal gateway; Varren fleet has unusually large ships; northern human timber settlements; monumental ancient Vanir stone remains. Dockside and household situations are illustrative social concepts, not new canonical events.
compliance.publicationAuthorization: Explicit user authorization for new canon-compatible social artwork and publication.
compliance.overlayMethod: Typeset locally using actual approved font after image generation; text anchored in screen space in Reel.
compliance.reelDirectionVersion: 2026-11-02 single scene with slow zoom and gentle text fade

pieces.title: The Visitors Brought Bigger Ships

validation.reviewMethod: Decoded all 420 encoded frames; temporal difference checked across the artwork region for jumps; encoded beginning, fade, middle, question and ending sampled visually at phone size. No audio generation; silent AAC track.

pieces.hypothesis: Scale contrast and an ordinary person's response to change, paired with a restrained single-scene zoom, will improve retention and follow conversion.

metadata.altText: A Rooan fisherman looks from a small fishing boat toward an enormous visiting Varren ship in Triport harbor.

request.text:
Their harbor suddenly felt very small.

Varren’s enormous ships have reached Roo. Imagine watching from a fishing boat: new trading partners, and a power you cannot match.

Would you welcome them or keep your distance?

The Land of Roo is an original Nordic fantasy world being created by Thomas Robbjens. Follow the continuing story.

Concept art from The Land of Roo.

#TheLandOfRoo #NordicFantasy #FantasyBooks #Worldbuilding

What changes when the visitors dwarf your boats?

Triport is Roo’s gateway to renewed contact by sea. The visiting fleet from Varren brings unusually large ships—and the possibility of diplomacy and trade.

This imagined dockside moment asks what that arrival might feel like to someone whose livelihood fits in a small fishing boat. Would you see an opportunity or a reason to be cautious?

The Land of Roo is an original Nordic fantasy world being created by Thomas Robbjens. Follow the continuing story.

Concept art from The Land of Roo.

#TheLandOfRoo #NordicFantasy #FantasyBooks #Worldbuilding

pieces.title: Boots or Grain?
pieces.hypothesis: Recognisable household stakes, consistent character and a concrete two-word choice will prompt swipes and meaningful responses.

request.text:
Warm feet, or food on the table?

Swipe to see what else is waiting on the counter.

An imagined everyday choice in Roo: replace the worn boots, or bring grain home and make the old pair last a little longer.

Which comes first—boots or grain?

Concept art from The Land of Roo.

#TheLandOfRoo #NordicFantasy #Worldbuilding #FantasyArt

metadata.altText: An auburn-haired Rooan woman considers new leather boots at a timber market stall, with her worn boots and a few coins visible. Text: She needs new boots. Swipe.
The same Rooan woman considers a sack of grain beside the new boots at the same market counter. Text: Her family needs grain. Boots or grain?

request.text:
Which need would you put first?

Beyond Roo’s ancient ruins and visiting fleets, someone still has to decide what to bring home from the market.

These two concept images imagine one household’s difficult purchase: sturdy boots for the days ahead, or grain for the family. Swipe to see both sides of the counter.

What would you choose first—boots or grain?

Concept art from The Land of Roo.

pieces.title: The Safest Crossing
pieces.hypothesis: A practical survival dilemma replaces a generic scenic description. It is explicitly imagined, without new ancient mechanisms or lore.

request.text:
The safest crossing can be no crossing.

Would You Survive Roo?

Imagine reaching this river mouth in the rain. The boat is still tied up: you can stay on shore. Across the water, an ancient doorway offers the promise of shelter—but reaching it means taking the boat out.

Would you wait by the landing or try for the doorway? Follow for tomorrow’s survival choice.

Concept art from The Land of Roo.

#TheLandOfRoo #NordicFantasy #Worldbuilding #FantasyArt

metadata.altText: A rain-darkened northern river mouth with a small fishing platform, boat, tiny traveler, and a monumental weathered stone doorway across the water.

request.text:
A doorway is not always an invitation.

Would You Survive Roo?

Imagine arriving here cold and soaked. A boat waits at the landing, and a monumental doorway overlooks the far bank. For now, the tied boat gives you a small victory: you still have the choice to stay ashore.

Would you wait beside the landing or risk the crossing for possible shelter? Which would you choose—and why?

Follow for tomorrow’s survival choice. Concept art from The Land of Roo.

#TheLandOfRoo #NordicFantasy #Worldbuilding #FantasyArt
